- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment >0.7.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and model forecasts rising, adjust downward by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence in reversal.
- If model forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome mean over 3–5 day horizon, apply 2–4% downward bias to next forecast window.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8, 0.2, 0.8), model often misreads momentum — use 3-day moving average of true prices to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 20% drop from peak), reduce forecast slope by 15–20% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and model forecasts high, assume “false breakout” — cap forecast at 10–15% below recent high.
